sources.section: Document Management - Institutional Repository and Digital Library Software
sources.entry: Fedora Commons Repository - Robust and modular repository system for the management and dissemination of digital content especially suited for digital libraries and archives, both for access and preservation. (Source Code) Apache-2.0 Java

summary.one_liner: Fedora is an open source, modular repository system for managing and disseminating digital content, aimed especially at digital libraries, archives, and preservation.
summary.what_it_does: Fedora is a Java-based repository server for storing, managing, and serving digital content. The README describes it as suited to digital libraries and archives for both access and preservation, and says it is also used for large, complex collections of historic, cultural, and scientific data. It exposes a REST API, and the README links to JavaDocs, technical docs, and a deployment guide. Stated technical goals include preservation storage layer transparency, scalability, flexible storage options, durability, and reporting/metrics. The project is stewarded by the Lyrasis organization.
use_cases: serve scientific datasets with a REST API
how_to_run: Deploy the war from ./fcrepo-webapp/target to a Jetty or Tomcat servlet container
Or for testing: cd fcrepo-webapp && mvn jetty:run
notable: Built for long-term digital preservation with storage layer transparency
Modular repository design deployable as a standard war file
REST API for managing and disseminating content
Backed by the Lyrasis organization with an established user base in universities and national libraries
caveats: Requires Java 21 and Maven 3.6.3 to build from source
Deployment needs a servlet container such as Jetty or Tomcat; jetty:run is described as a testing method
